Legend Barber

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
It all Started on the streets of Eldorado Park, Sheldon Tatchell was a kid with a dream, and mad skillz for cutting fresh cuts. Today he is a business mogul with 50 stores nationwide and legends like American rapper Usher and South African Super star Ricky rick as brands ambassadors.

But where does the name come from? When they weren’t cutting hair on the streets Sheldon and his boys used to go to old age homes. “To hang out, listen to the wisdom and give everyone cuts for free. I felt like they were the legends, so we called our store legends” They still do this monthly. Giving back to the community is one of the things that Sheldon equates to his success. Besides going to old age homes, they also go to schools in low-income areas and give the kids expensive cuts for free.

The second reason for his success he says is customer service, “If you make people feel seen and cared for, they will come back” Sheldon used to have a book where he would write down the conversations he had with clients, so that he could pick up where they left off the next time, they came in.

It wasn’t always smooth sailing though; he had a partner who bounced leaving the business in Ruins. But he got back up and opened Legends, on his won, in 2014.
Sheldon’s story is a classic rag to riches narrative, he is like the Jay Z of haircuts, from the streets to the highlife.

As a kid Sheldon TATCHELL roamed the streets looking for ways to make money, he didn’t want to be a gangster so he started shadowing the only other top business guys in his area, the local barbers

the barber was basically the person that you go to every week
and the guys that came up with the coolest haircut the praise used to go to the barber instead of the person. And that actually made the barber the coolest guy in in the community.

When Sheldon was 14 years old instead of getting clothes for Christmas his father saved enough money to buy his son his first pair of clippers
And For the rest of his teenage years Sheldon became the kid that everyone went to after school for the freshest haircuts.

I mean, at age of 14 years old
I'll be on the street going to go hustle something.
I can remember there was a time where both my parents were working.
and that used to contribute to the house where I lived him.. So that actually contribute to me providing for the family.

In less than ten years Sheldon Tatchell built a barbershop empire with over 60 STORES across Africa

it's not something that I could imagine
If you would've told me that you'll be in control of to 500 staff members. I never thought that would be possible.

But building his empire has not been an overnight success for Sheldon. After finishing school his dream was to open his own Barber shop, but he didn’t have the capital and his parents insisted he get a real job. So he started working in the bamk

it was a nine to five job where you were able to day you wake up and you feel miserable and you question yourself each and every day, Is it having an impact on the community? Am I making a difference

Even though from Monday to Friday he dragged himself to his bank job.
on Saturday and Sunday Sheldon setup a chair, an extension cable and a boom box outside his cousins computer shop in Eldorado PARK and he did what made him happy, he cut hair

I always believed that that in order to run the business, you have to be creative.
I used to have a small notebook and write on each and every customer's name and the conversation that we added the long.
So next time that person would come back and sit in the chair, I would make reference to the booklet
So you just continue on that relationship building. And thats been the foundation of legends ever since.

After years of working in the bank and cutting hair as a side hustle in 2014 Sheldon made the decision to quit the bank and invest everything he had into opening his barbershop in eldos. He worked 27/7 to create a name for the business and for the first 4 months he never took a cent home

there was no investors ever since I started
I've learned the hard way
you tend to cherish it a bit more. And then you tend to look at every penny and understand and each and every dime counts

While Sheldon put every cent he earned back into the barbershop, his wife Elvira Tatchell become the bread winner in the family.

she was she was a person that said, You know what? She will get it across the board now, so she will make sure that we at least have stuff to eat. Fortunately for us, back then, we didn't have kids,
she stood by me all the way.

Sheldon is a
very strange way of getting into your heart.
Oh, how can I say it out of about to describe him? Very persistent, yeah
He describes himself as a kind, and I'm the person that keeps us grounded

A year after opening his first store Sheldon open a second and a year after that a third, and within his first 3 years he had opened 6 stores nationwide
It was only at this point that he actually started to draw a real salary, equivalent to what he had been earning in the bank, from the barbershop business

My main objective was that I'm not going to be able to pay my salary with one store because it wouldn't be feasible. So I had to double it up. I had to put money back into the business.
And that's a formula that I was using all along is just putting money back into the business, back into the business and just seeing how it goes from there.

Just like the barbers he use to shadow on the streets of Eldo’s Sheldon Tatchell has now become a Celebrity Barber in his own right. He is the go to guy for Heavy weight celebrities across South Africa.

The celebrities caught on to the wave that we were trying to build, and and I know it sounds a bit arrogant,
celebrities wanted to be part of legends and it wasn't the other way around them. Like we went running after celebrities, celebrities would basically call us out and ask us,
Can we give them a haircut to understand

Celebrities like Ricky rick started getting their cuts done by Sheldon and then posting about it on social media

social media has played a big part in our business
I think 80 percent of business is based on social media and that that is that is based on word of mouth, people posting people just checking in at the nearest nations

If you speak to anyone that has ever met Sheldon they will tell that this empire he is building is his life, and the bigger its gets the harder he works.

Sheldon wakes up extremely early.
Four o'clock, three o'clock. He sends out messages. His brain is always running, making sure that we are always one step ahead of the rest.
He sacrifices family time. He sacrifices personal time
to make sure to make sure that this business runs as efficiently as it does.

I try to keep our family life afloat
try to maintain a good relationship with our kids.
Make sure that they know that is out working. Yeah, and I try to basically just stand in for him. Most of the time. I'm emotional because I think of All the sacrifices that were made to get the business rate is and

It's not the normal lifestyle. I mean, my kids sometimes they don't understand. what you're trying to do is to build something that will surpass their lifetimes
coming up with nothing. It made me more angry. It made me more. It made me want to have more, you understand, because I wouldn't want my kids to grab the same that I grew up
I would like to provide them for better education, for a better future than what I had







For Sheldon business isn’t just about MAKING money, it is about building a legacy of serving HIS community.

always believe that that that if you're a blessing to others, you'll be blessed.
if you give up negativity, negativity is going to come back. But if you give out good, good, it's going to come back to you. And and that's something that we've loved by as a business being able to always do good in other people's lives.

When that light is looking through that school window, yes, thinking about the future. Yes, hoping to be an India for now? Yes. What did you say to him? You know, what did you say to Young Sheldon? Yes, you know that I said that that wants to travel this journey.

Yeah, I would say I would say, never stop dreaming. Never stop dreaming. I mean, for me personally, it was it was really tough. You understand for us because you come from a place where you come from, a place where where people around you don't talk about places like your and you don't get out of this mentality of the four corners of the Eldorado Park. Understand. So you don't look out of the scope you understand because you you're so glued into what's happening in your community and you and you, it limits you to bring a bond beyond that, that awkwardness.

And and that's one thing I would say is that that your dreams are valid
